A feed that parses but has no future events is STALE, not empty. Feeds are
re-checked every run, so a source going stale is reported, never silently
dropped. Confirmed stale feeds are kept here with enabled:false and a note,
so we do not rediscover and re-trust them later.

Connecticut was invisible for a different reason than distance: Danbury is 27.8 mi from Beacon and was always inside the radius, but the registry had no CT sources at all. Coverage gaps look like radius gaps — check the registry before widening the circle.

Eventbrite and Meetup were previously assumed to need paid API access. Both hand their front end public JSON, which is why the registry now carries them: check what a site gives its own browser before concluding there is no free path.

Localist runs the calendar at events.<domain>/calendar.ics, not on the main domain, so no FEED_PATHS probe reaches it. discover.py now tries that host directly — six college feeds came from that one pattern.

campus:true marks a college calendar. Those are internal by default — orientation, registration, finals, involvement fairs — so merge.py keeps only what is genuinely open to the public (a lecture, concert, gallery opening, mass, 5K) plus home games, and drops the rest. An allowlist, not a blocklist: chasing "Viking Days" and "Pie a Kappa" by name never ends.

LibCal is read by scripts/libcal.py, not the registry: its iCal export returns an empty body and rss.php a feed with zero items, so the only working route is the per-day ajax endpoint the calendar page itself calls, walked day by day.

Songkick is read by scripts/songkick.py (metro pages, JSON-LD MusicEvents): the ticketed-concert layer — Capitol Theatre, Tarrytown Music Hall, Daryl's House — whose own sites bot-challenge us or render in JavaScript. Their search/API endpoints 406; the metro pages serve plain HTML.

Marist has a working Liferay JSON API at /api/jsonws/events.maristevent/get-upcoming-events/limit/1000 (double-encoded JSON), but every entry is internal academic calendar — Semester Begins, Search Committee Meeting, Open House. Not registered: the campus rule would drop all of it.

Assabet Interactive is the other library calendar platform beside LibCal, and it does publish schema.org Events on /calendar/. Its subdomain is not derivable from the library domain — fingerprint the homepage for an assabetinteractive.com link instead.

Local cinemas are the hardest tier in the registry. Twenty-three were probed in the 2026-08 pass and one — the Fisher Center at Bard — had a feed. The rest run bespoke or client-side ticketing (Filmbot, Wix Thunderbolt, Veezi) with no iCal, no JSON-LD and no public API, so they are html and hand-read. Do not re-probe them hoping for a feed.

downingfilmcenter.com is NOT the Downing Film Center any more: the domain now serves an Indonesian gambling site (215 mentions of "slot", none of "Downing" or "Newburgh"). It is deliberately absent from this registry — a hand-read pass must not ingest it. Find the theatre's current home before adding it back.

storyscreenbeacon.com is NOT Story Screen any more: the domain now serves a Turkish gambling site (14 gambling markers, zero mentions of "Story Screen", "Beacon", "movie" or "film"). Story Screen itself is alive at storyscreenpresents.com, which is what this registry points at.
bethelcinema.com is NOT Bethel Cinema any more: the domain now serves an Indonesian togel/gambling storefront. It is deliberately absent from this registry.

rivertownfilm.org (Nyack) is a live site with real listings, but its WordPress has been SEO-spammed — paragraphs of Australian online-casino copy sit in the page body beside the film blurbs. Not registered: anything read off it would carry the spam into descriptions.

Three theatre domains in one 50-mile pass had lapsed and been re-registered by gambling operators (downingfilmcenter.com, storyscreenbeacon.com, bethelcinema.com). Small venues lose domains often, so a cinema URL that has not been fetched in a while is worth re-checking for content, not just for HTTP status — all three answer 200.

Of roughly two dozen independent cinemas inside fifty miles, five serve their schedule as HTML (Jacob Burns, Rosendale, and the three Independent Cinemas houses) and are read by scripts/cinema.py. The rest run a ticketing SPA — Indy Systems, Filmbot's hosted app, or Agile Ticketing behind Imperva — and are hand-read or disabled.

Places are collected at placesRadiusMiles (50), not the 100-mile event radius. An event is worth travelling for on a given night; a garden or an antique shop is a Sunday, and 100 miles of OpenStreetMap is tens of thousands of rows nobody scrolls.

The place taxonomy lives in scripts/placekinds.py and nowhere else. enrich.py reads it as name patterns (an event only tells us what its venue is called) and places.py reads it as OpenStreetMap tag rules; both name the same 26 kinds, and an import-time assert fails if either names one the list does not define.

Read by hand into sources/manual.json. Their pop-up screenings run at breweries and parks rather than at one address, so each listing carries its own venue. NOTE the domain change: storyscreenbeacon.com is no longer theirs and must not be fetched — see the hijack note above.

Filmbot. The month grid is server-rendered and each day cell carries the whole show card in an escaped data-show-card attribute — title, link, blurb and that day's times. Month navigation is the path /calendar/YYYY-MM, not a query parameter. Read by scripts/cinema.py.
Indy Systems SPA (Quasar). The 8KB shell talks to a same-origin /graphql endpoint; nothing is in the served HTML. No hand-read path either — the listing pages render entirely in JS.

12KB shell to a scripted fetch; the listing renders client-side. Read by hand into sources/manual.json — only the screenings whose exact date and time the page spells out. Multi-day runs are listed without per-day times and are deliberately skipped rather than guessed at.

Wix. Showtimes come from the Thunderbolt renderer, and the Agile Ticketing schedule behind it sits behind an Imperva bot wall, so neither is fetchable. The /events page does render its special screenings as text — read by hand into sources/manual.json.
Client-rendered listings. 55 mi out — inside the event radius, outside the 50-mile cinema pass.

Every showtime carries an ISO data-showtime attribute in the served HTML. A rolling three-day window that ignores ?date=, so a weekly run keeps it current and there is nothing to page. Read by scripts/cinema.py.

One small operator runs three Hudson Valley houses off one server-rendered page each: a date header, then alternating title and times lines. Times carry no meridiem because a cinema day starts at noon. Read by scripts/cinema.py.
